claims.statement: The pinned note describes issue forms as public preview and changeable. This historical phase is not current live availability or template stability certification.

The example issue form declares name/description/title, labels, projects, assignees and issue type, using source-specific example identities. These are unadopted placeholders requiring target applicability and authorization, not valid real project assignments or an installed form.

The sample makes contact optional, requires problem description and version selection, supplies an illustrative indexed default version, allows multiple browser selections, and formats optional log text as shell code. Required/default fields do not verify the truth of a report; formatting is not safe execution or secret redaction. Contact and logs can contain private data, so no real submissions were acquired.

The sample requires a code-of-conduct checkbox using an example link and conditionally offers optional screenshot upload only under issue-form-upload. A checked box is submitted attestation, not verified compliance; preserve the conditional feature branch and do not treat unrendered Liquid/YAML as universally deployable. No template was adopted or run.

The report procedure offers repository-admin versus platform-support routing when available, otherwise advances to the next contextual step. Repository-admin reason selection and the Report content/Send request flow are different branches, not proof both happen or a real report was submitted. Source prose saying submitted is an example outcome, not an agent receipt; no report or external message was sent.

The temporary interaction-limit step selects an enable dropdown for the chosen limit type and duration. It is a configuration procedure, not authorization to moderate, proof of effective restrictions or specification of the affected audience; prior duration and operation claims retain separate scope.
